title: Intersection of Two Arrays
question: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, return an array of their intersection. Each element in the result must be unique and you may return the result in any order.

title: Happy Number
question: Write an algorithm to determine if a number n is happy. A happy number is defined by: starting with any positive integer, keep replacing the number by the sum of the squares of its digits until it equals 1 or loops endlessly. Use a set to detect cycles.

title: Isomorphic Strings
question: Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic. Two strings are isomorphic if the characters in s can be replaced to get t. All occurrences of a character must be replaced with another character while preserving the order.
constraints: s and t consist of any valid ascii character

title: Word Pattern
question: Given a pattern and a string s, find if s follows the pattern. Here, 'follow' means a full match, such that there is a bijection between a letter in pattern and a non-empty word in s.
constraints: pattern contains only lower-case English letters
s contains only lowercase English letters and spaces ' '

title: First Unique Character in String
question: Given a string s, find the first non-repeating character and return its index. If no such character exists, return -1.
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters

title: Contains Duplicate
question: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.

title: Group Anagrams
question: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order. An anagram is a word formed by rearranging the letters of another.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters

title: Top K Frequent Elements
question: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order. Use a hash map to count frequencies and a heap for top k elements.
constraints: k is in the range [1, number of unique elements]

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
question: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Use a sliding window with a hash set to track characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
question: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals k. Use prefix sums with a hash map.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
question: Implement a RandomizedSet class with insert, remove, and getRandom operations, all in average O(1) time. Use a hash map and an array.

title: Minimum Window Substring
question: Given two strings s and t, return the minimum window in s which will contain all the characters in t. Use a hash map and sliding window.
constraints: s and t consist of English letters

title: Valid Sudoku
question: Determine if a 9 x 9 Sudoku board is valid. Only the filled cells need to be validated according to the following rules: Each row contains digits 1-9 without repetition, each column contains digits 1-9 without repetition, and each 3x3 sub-box contains digits 1-9 without repetition.

title: Majority Element II
question: Given an integer array of size n, find all elements that appear more than n/3 times. There can be at most 2 such elements. Use a hash map.

title: 4Sum II
question: Given four lists of integers nums1, nums2, nums3, nums4, count the number of tuples (i, j, k, l) where nums1[i] + nums2[j] + nums3[k] + nums4[l] == 0. Use hash map to combine first two arrays.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring with Hashing
question: Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring. Use rolling hash (polynomial rolling hash) to optimize palindrome detection.
constraints: s consist of only digits and English letters

title: Word Ladder
question: Given two words, beginWord and endWord, find the length of the shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord such that only one letter can be changed at a time. Use BFS with a hash set.

title: Design Search Autocomplete System
question: Design a search autocomplete system for a search engine. User types character by character and you return top 3 search sentences historically ranked by frequency. Use a trie and hash map.

title: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
question: Given an array of equations and a list of variables, determine if it's possible to assign values to variables such that all equations are satisfied. Use Union-Find with a hash map.

title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
question: Given a string containing English words for digits ('zero', 'one', ..., 'nine'), remove them and return the digits in order. Use a hash map to count letters.
constraints: s[i] is lower case English letter

title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
question: Given a 1-indexed array of integers numbers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers that add up to a specific target number. Use two pointers from both ends.

title: Valid Palindrome
question: Given a string s, determine if it is a palindrome, considering only alphanumeric characters and ignoring cases. Use two pointers.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters

title: Reverse String
question: Write a function that reverses a string in-place. Do not allocate extra space for another array; you must modify the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
constraints: s[i] is a printable ascii character

title: Merge Sorted Array
question: You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, merge them into a single array sorted in non-decreasing order. You must modify nums1 in-place and use O(1) extra space. Use two pointers from the ends.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
question: Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order, remove duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. Use two pointers.

title: Is Number a Palindrome
question: Given an integer x, return true if x is a palindrome, and false otherwise. A palindrome is a number that reads the same backward as forward.

title: Backspace String Compare
question: Given two strings s and t, return true if they are equal when both are typed into empty text editors. '#' means a backspace character. Use two pointers from the end.
constraints: s and t only contain lowercase letters and '#' characters

title: Move Zeroes
question: Given an integer array nums, move all zeroes to the end while maintaining the relative order of non-zero elements. Use two pointers.

title: 3Sum
question: Given an integer array nums of length n, find all unique triplets that sum to 0. Return the result as a list of unique triplets. Sort the array first, then use two pointers for each element.

title: Container With Most Water
question: You are given an integer array height of length n. Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that can hold the most water. Return the maximum area you can obtain. Use two pointers from both ends.

title: Trapping Rain Water
question: Given an elevation map represented by an array height, compute how much water can be trapped after raining. Use two pointers to track the water level.

title: Partition Labels
question: You are given a string s. You want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part. Return a list of the size of each partition. Use two pointers with a hash map.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
question: Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer target, find the minimal length of a subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to target. Use a sliding window with two pointers.

title: Sort Colors
question: Given an array nums with n objects colored red (0), white (1), or blue (2), sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent. Use two or three pointers (Dutch National Flag problem).

title: Rotate Array
question: Given an array, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative. Use the reverse method with two pointers.

title: Interval List Intersections
question: Given two lists of intervals as input where each interval is exclusive at the end, find the intersection of the two interval lists. Use two pointers.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
question: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return the head of the modified list. Use two pointers with n nodes gap.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
question: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 of size m and n respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays. The median should be calculated using two pointers for O(log(m+n)) optimization.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
question: Given an array of integers heights representing the histogram heights, find the largest rectangle area that can be formed. Use a monotonic stack or two pointers with preprocessing.

title: Maximal Rectangle
question: Given a rows x cols binary matrix filled with 0s and 1s, find the largest rectangle containing only 1s and return its area. Use histogram approach with two pointers.

title: Critical Connections in Network
question: There are n servers numbered from 0 to n-1 connected in a network with vertices and edges. A critical connection is a connection that will cause the network to have a disconnected component if removed. Find all critical connections using DFS with two pointers concept (discovery and low-link values).

title: Shortest Substring Containing All Characters
question: Given a string s and a string t, find the shortest continuous substring of s that contains all the characters in t. Use a sliding window with two pointers.

title: Vertical Order Traversal with Two Pointers
question: Given a binary tree, return the vertical order traversal of its nodes. Nodes at the same horizontal distance appear in the same column. Use a column-based approach with hash map and two pointers for sorting.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 100]

title: Find Closest Number to Zero
question: Given an integer array nums of size n, find the number closest to zero. If there are multiple answers, return the number with the greatest absolute value. Use two pointers.

title: Water Bottles II with Pointers
question: You have n full water bottles and you can exchange empty bottles for full ones. Each full bottle has capacity c. Find total water drunk using two pointers to track progress.

title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
question: Given an array of integers and a positive integer k, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of size exactly k. Use a fixed-size sliding window to solve it in O(n) time.

title: Average of All Subarrays of Size K
question: Given an array of integers and a positive integer k, return an array of the averages of all contiguous subarrays of size k. Round averages to 5 decimal places.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
question: Given an array of positive integers and a target sum, find the minimal length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is >= target. Return 0 if no such subarray exists. Use a variable-size sliding window in O(n).

title: First Negative Number in Every Window of Size K
question: Given an array and a positive integer k, for each window of size k find the first negative number. If no negative exists in a window, output 0 for that window. Return the result array.

title: Count Occurrences of Anagrams
question: Given a text string txt and a pattern string pat, count the number of occurrences of anagrams of pat in txt. An anagram is a permutation of the pattern. Use a fixed sliding window of size pat.length with frequency comparison.
constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters

title: Max Consecutive Ones III
question: Given a binary array and an integer k, return the maximum number of consecutive 1s if you can flip at most k zeroes. The window expands right; when zeros inside exceed k, shrink from the left.

title: Longest Subarray of Ones After Deleting One Element
question: Given a binary array, delete exactly one element. Return the size of the longest non-empty subarray containing only 1s in the resulting array. Equivalent to finding the longest window with at most one 0.

title: Diet Plan Performance
question: Given a calorie array and integers k, lower, upper, calculate a performance score: for each window of k days, add +1 if sum > upper, -1 if sum < lower, 0 otherwise. Return the total performance score.

title: Subarray Product Less Than K
question: Given an array of positive integers and integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays where the product of all elements is strictly less than k. Use a variable-size sliding window.

title: Sliding Window Maximum - Fixed Size
question: Given an integer array and a window size k, return an array of the maximum value in each sliding window. Use a deque to maintain decreasing order, giving O(n) time.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
question: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Use a sliding window with a hash map to track last-seen positions of each character. O(n) time.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols, and spaces

title: Fruit Into Baskets
question: You have a row of trees, each bearing fruit of type arr[i]. You have exactly 2 baskets, each holding one fruit type (unlimited quantity). Starting from any tree, pick fruits from consecutive trees. Find the maximum number of fruits you can pick. Equivalent to the longest subarray with at most 2 distinct values.

title: Permutation in String
question: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1 as a substring. Maintain a fixed window of size s1.length in s2 and compare frequency arrays. O(n) solution expected.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters

title: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
question: Given a string s and an integer k, return the maximum number of vowel letters in any substring of s with length k. Use a fixed-size sliding window tracking vowel count.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

title: Minimum Window Substring
question: Given strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included. If no such window exists, return an empty string. Use two pointers + frequency map.
constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
question: Given a string s and integer k, you can replace at most k characters. Find the length of the longest substring containing the same letter after replacements. Key insight: window is valid when (window_size - max_freq) <= k.
constraints: s consists of uppercase English letters

title: Maximum Points You Can Obtain from Cards
question: Given a row of cards with integer scores, you can take exactly k cards from either end (left or right). Maximize the total score. Equivalent to finding the minimum sum window of size (n-k) in the middle.

title: Count Number of Nice Subarrays
question: Given an array of integers and integer k, a subarray is 'nice' if there are exactly k odd numbers in it. Return the count of nice subarrays. Use a sliding window counting technique: count(exactly k) = count(at most k) - count(at most k-1).

title: Longest Subarray with Sum at Most K
question: Given an array of non-negative integers and integer k, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is at most k. Use a variable-size sliding window that shrinks from the left when sum exceeds k.

title: Maximum Sum of Two Non-Overlapping Subarrays
question: Given an integer array nums and integers firstLen and secondLen, return the maximum sum of elements in two non-overlapping subarrays of lengths firstLen and secondLen respectively. Try all splits: first subarray comes before second and vice versa.

title: Minimum Window Containing All Distinct Characters
question: Given a string s, find the length of the smallest substring that contains all distinct characters of s. Use a sliding window tracking how many unique characters in the current window have reached their full frequency.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
question: Given an integer array nums and integer k, return the number of subarrays with exactly k distinct integers. Use atMost(k) - atMost(k-1) technique where atMost(k) counts subarrays with at most k distinct values.

title: Minimum Swaps to Group All 1s Together II
question: A circular binary array means the next element of the last element is the first. Return the minimum number of swaps needed to group all 1s together anywhere in the circular array. Use a fixed window of size = total_ones, find the window with maximum 1s already inside.

title: Maximum Erasure Value
question: You are given an array of positive integers. You want to erase a subarray containing unique elements. The score you get by erasing the subarray is equal to the sum of its elements. Return the maximum score you can get by erasing exactly one subarray.

title: Longest Continuous Subarray with Absolute Diff at Most Limit
question: Given an integer array nums and integer limit, return the size of the longest subarray where the absolute difference between any two elements is <= limit. Maintain a max-deque and min-deque simultaneously to track current window min/max in O(1).

title: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
question: Given a string s consisting only of 'a', 'b', and 'c', return the number of substrings containing at least one occurrence of all three characters. For every right endpoint, find the leftmost valid window start and count all valid endings. O(n).

title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
question: Given an integer array and integer x, each operation removes the leftmost or rightmost element and subtracts it from x. Return the minimum number of operations to reduce x to exactly 0, or -1 if impossible. Equivalent to finding the longest subarray with sum = (totalSum - x).

title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
question: Given a string s and integer k, find the length of the longest substring with at most k distinct characters. Maintain a character frequency map; when distinct count exceeds k, shrink from left.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K (with Negatives)
question: Given an integer array (may include negatives) and integer k, return the length of the shortest non-empty subarray with sum >= k. Use prefix sums + monotonic deque for O(n log n) solution.

title: Sliding Window Median
question: Given an integer array and window size k, return an array of medians for each sliding window. Maintain two heaps (max-heap for lower half, min-heap for upper half) supporting O(log k) inserts/deletes per step.

title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
question: Given an integer array, implement a NumArray class supporting sumRange(left, right) returning the sum of elements between indices left and right (inclusive). Precompute prefix sums so each query is O(1).

title: Find the Middle Index in Array
question: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, find the leftmost middle index i such that the sum of elements to the left of i equals the sum to the right of i. Return i, or -1 if no such index exists. Left sum of index 0 and right sum of last index are both 0.

title: Running Sum of 1D Array
question: Given an array nums, return an array where runningSum[i] = sum(nums[0]...nums[i]). This is the prefix sum array itself. Compute in O(n) in a single pass.

title: Check if Array Pairs Are Divisible by K
question: Given an array of integers and integer k, check if you can divide the array into n/2 pairs such that the sum of each pair is divisible by k. Use a frequency array of remainders: remainder r must pair with (k-r), and remainder 0 must pair with itself.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
question: Given an integer array and integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals k. Use a prefix sum + hash map: count how many previous prefix sums equal (current prefix sum - k).

title: Product of Array Except Self
question: Given an integer array, return an output array where output[i] is the product of all elements except nums[i]. Solve without division in O(n) using a prefix product array (left products) and a suffix product pass.
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Find Pivot Index
question: Find the pivot index of an array: the index where the sum of all elements to its left equals the sum of all elements to its right. Return the leftmost such index, or -1 if none. Compute total sum, then track left sum as you iterate.

title: XOR Queries of a Subarray
question: Given an array arr and queries [Li, Ri], return an array of answers where answer[i] = XOR of arr[Li] to arr[Ri]. Precompute prefix XOR array: prefix[i] = arr[0] XOR ... XOR arr[i-1]. Then query = prefix[Ri+1] XOR prefix[Li].

title: Sum of Even Numbers After Queries
question: Given array nums and queries where each query is [val, index], add val to nums[index] then return the sum of all even elements. Maintain a running even sum; update it when a queried element's parity changes.

title: Check Array Formation Through Concatenation
question: Given an array arr and an array of chunks, return true if you can form arr by concatenating these chunks in some order (each used exactly once). Build a hash map from first element of each chunk to the chunk, then greedily match.
constraints: All elements of arr are unique

title: Contiguous Array
question: Given a binary array, find the maximum length contiguous subarray with an equal number of 0s and 1s. Replace 0s with -1s and find the longest subarray with sum 0 using a prefix sum + hash map.

title: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
question: Given an integer array and integer k, find the maximum length of a subarray that sums to k. Use prefix sum + hash map storing the first occurrence index of each prefix sum. Answer is max(i - firstIndex[prefixSum - k]).

title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
question: Given a 2D matrix, handle multiple sumRegion(r1,c1,r2,c2) queries returning the sum of elements in the rectangle bounded by the corners. Precompute a 2D prefix sum matrix for O(1) per query. prefix[i][j] = sum of rectangle (0,0) to (i-1,j-1).

title: Continuous Subarray Sum
question: Given an integer array and integer k, return true if the array has a continuous subarray of length >= 2 whose sum is a multiple of k. Use prefix sum mod k: if two indices have the same prefix sum mod k and their distance >= 2, the subarray between them is divisible by k.

title: Count Subarrays with Score Less Than K
question: The score of a non-empty subarray is defined as length * sum. Given an integer array and long integer k, return the count of non-empty subarrays with score strictly less than k. Use prefix sums + binary search for each right endpoint.

title: Path Sum III
question: Given a binary tree root and integer targetSum, return the number of paths that sum to targetSum. Paths go downward (from parent to child) but need not start at root or end at a leaf. Use DFS with prefix sum hash map: count[currentSum - targetSum] gives valid completions.
constraints: The tree has at most 1000 nodes

title: Number of Ways to Split Array
question: Given an integer array, count the number of valid split indices i (0 <= i < n-1) where the sum of the first i+1 elements >= sum of the remaining elements. Precompute total sum; iterate tracking prefix sum to check condition in O(n).

title: Count Number of Bad Pairs
question: A pair (i, j) is bad if i < j and j - i != nums[j] - nums[i]. Return the number of bad pairs. Key insight: a pair is GOOD if nums[i] - i == nums[j] - j. Count good pairs using a frequency map of (nums[i] - i), then bad = total - good.

title: Make Sum Divisible by P
question: Given an array of positive integers and integer p, remove the smallest subarray (possibly empty) such that the sum of the remaining elements is divisible by p. Return its length or -1 if impossible. Use prefix sum mod p + hash map: find subarray whose sum ≡ (total % p) mod p.

title: Maximum Sum of Subarray with Length Between L and R
question: Given an integer array and integers l, r, find the maximum sum of a contiguous subarray with length between l and r (inclusive). Use prefix sums and maintain a sliding window minimum of prefix[i-l..i-r] as you traverse.

title: Count of Range Sum
question: Given an integer array and two integers lower and upper, return the number of range sums S(i, j) such that lower <= S(i, j) <= upper. Use a sorted prefix sum + merge sort or balanced BST. O(n log n).

title: Maximum Sum Rectangle in a 2D Matrix
question: Given an m x n matrix, find the sub-rectangle with the maximum sum. Compress each pair of rows into a 1D problem, then apply Kadane's algorithm on the column prefix sums. O(m^2 * n).

title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
question: Given array (possibly with negatives) and integer k, return the length of the shortest subarray with sum >= k. Build prefix sums, then use a monotonic deque: pop from front when valid, pop from back while prefix[back] >= prefix[right] (not useful).

title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
question: Given an m x n matrix and integer target, return the number of non-empty submatrices that sum to target. Enumerate all pairs of rows; compress each row range to a 1D array and use prefix sum + hash map to count subarrays equaling target.

title: Stamping the Grid
question: Given an m x n binary grid and stamp dimensions stampHeight x stampWidth, determine if you can cover all empty (0) cells using stamps (which may overlap but cannot cover occupied (1) cells). Use 2D prefix sums twice: first to check no occupied cell under stamp, then to verify all empty cells are covered.

title: Maximum Score of Non-Overlapping Intervals with Prefix Sum
question: Given a sorted array and query intervals [l, r, weight], select at most k non-overlapping intervals to maximize total weight * (range sum). For each right boundary, binary search for the last non-overlapping interval's DP value. O(n log n).

title: Maximum White Tiles Covered by a Carpet
question: Given a list of non-overlapping white tile intervals and a carpet of length carpetLen, return the maximum number of white tiles covered by placing the carpet optimally. Sort intervals, build prefix sums, then binary search for each placement start.

title: Longest Well-Performing Interval
question: A day is tiring if hours > 8. Find the longest interval (subarray) that is well-performing: more tiring days than non-tiring days. Convert to +1/-1 and use prefix sum + hash map: for prefix[i] > 0 the whole prefix is valid; otherwise find the earliest j where prefix[j] = prefix[i] - 1.

title: Number of Substrings with Only 1s
question: Given a binary string, return the number of substrings that consist only of '1's. For each run of k consecutive '1's, it contributes k*(k+1)/2 substrings. Sum contributions modulo 10^9+7. Use prefix sum approach tracking current consecutive 1s count.

title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
question: Given an integer array, find the sum over all subarrays of (max - min). Naive is O(n^2); optimal uses two monotonic stacks to compute the contribution of each element as max minus its contribution as min. O(n).

title: Binary Search
question: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target, implement classic binary search. Return the index of target, or -1 if not found. Must run in O(log n).
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order

title: Search Insert Position
question: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target, return the index if found, or the index where it would be inserted to maintain sorted order. Must run in O(log n).
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order

title: First and Last Position in Sorted Array
question: Given a sorted array (with duplicates) and a target, find the starting and ending positions using two binary searches (lower bound and upper bound). Return [-1, -1] if not found. O(log n).
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

title: Sqrt(x) Using Binary Search
question: Given a non-negative integer x, return the integer square root (floor of sqrt(x)) without using built-in sqrt functions. Binary search on [0, x]: find largest mid such that mid*mid <= x. O(log x).

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
question: Given a sorted array rotated at some pivot (all elements unique), find the minimum element using binary search. Compare mid with right: if arr[mid] > arr[right], minimum is in the right half, otherwise in the left. O(log n).

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
question: A sorted array was rotated at an unknown pivot (all distinct values). Given the rotated array and a target, return its index or -1. Determine which half is sorted using mid vs boundary comparison, then narrow down. O(log n).

title: Guess Number Higher or Lower
question: A number is picked from 1 to n. You call guess(num) returning -1 (too high), 1 (too low), or 0 (correct). Find the picked number using binary search. O(log n) calls required.

title: Peak Index in a Mountain Array
question: A mountain array strictly increases then strictly decreases. Find the peak index using binary search: if arr[mid] < arr[mid+1], peak is to the right; otherwise to the left. O(log n).
constraints: Guaranteed to be a mountain array

title: Count Occurrences in Sorted Array
question: Given a sorted array and a target value, return the number of times the target appears. Use binary search (upper_bound - lower_bound) to achieve O(log n).
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

title: Check If N and Its Double Exist
question: Given an integer array, check if there exist two indices i != j such that arr[i] == 2 * arr[j]. Sort the array then for each element use binary search to find its double. Handle the zero case carefully (0 == 2*0 needs two separate zeros).

title: Koko Eating Bananas
question: Koko can eat at most k bananas per hour. Given piles and h hours, find the minimum integer k so she can finish all bananas in h hours. Binary search k in [1, max(piles)]; check feasibility by summing ceil(pile/k) for each pile.

title: Capacity to Ship Packages Within D Days
question: Given weights of packages (in order) and D days, find the minimum ship capacity to ship all packages within D days. Binary search on capacity: lo = max(weights), hi = sum(weights). Greedy check: simulate loading with given capacity.

title: Find K Closest Elements
question: Given a sorted integer array, integers k and x, return the k closest integers to x in ascending order. Ties favor smaller. Binary search for left boundary: lo=0, hi=n-k; compare |arr[mid]-x| vs |arr[mid+k]-x|. O(log(n-k) + k).
constraints: arr is sorted in ascending order

title: Find Kth Smallest Element in Sorted Matrix
question: Given an n x n matrix where each row and column is sorted ascending, find the kth smallest element. Binary search on value range [matrix[0][0], matrix[n-1][n-1]]: count elements <= mid using pointer starting at top-right. O(n log(max-min)).
constraints: All rows and columns are sorted

title: Single Element in a Sorted Array
question: In a sorted array, every element appears exactly twice except one. Find that single element in O(log n) time and O(1) space. Key insight: before the single element, pairs start at even indices; after it, pairs start at odd indices.

title: Magnetic Force Between Two Balls
question: Place m balls into sorted basket positions to maximize the minimum magnetic force (minimum distance) between any two balls. Binary search on the answer: check feasibility greedily (place next ball only when distance >= mid). O(n log n).

title: Search a 2D Matrix
question: An m x n matrix has rows sorted ascending and each row's first element is greater than the last of the previous row. Given a target, return whether it exists. Treat as a 1D sorted array of m*n elements and apply binary search. O(log(m*n)).

title: Minimum Rotations to Open Lock
question: A lock has 4 circular dials (0-9). Starting at '0000', find the minimum turns to reach the target, avoiding deadends. Each turn changes one digit by +1 or -1 (mod 10). Use BFS; include binary search insight for state-space search. Return -1 if target unreachable.
constraints: target will not be in deadends
target and deadend[i] consist of digits only

title: Split Array Largest Sum
question: Split an integer array into k non-empty contiguous subarrays to minimize the largest subarray sum. Binary search on answer in [max(nums), sum(nums)]; check using greedy simulation whether a given max sum allows at most k splits.

title: Allocate Minimum Number of Pages
question: Given book page counts and m students, allocate contiguous books to students minimizing the maximum pages any student reads. Binary search on answer: lo = max(books), hi = sum(books). Greedy check counts required students for a given capacity.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
question: Given two sorted arrays, return the median of the combined sorted array. Binary search on the smaller array to find a partition such that all left elements <= all right elements across both arrays. O(log(min(m, n))).

title: Find in Mountain Array
question: A mountain array strictly increases then decreases. Given a MountainArray interface and a target, find the minimum index where value == target using at most 100 API calls. Step 1: binary search for peak. Step 2: binary search ascending side. Step 3: binary search descending side.

title: K-th Smallest Number in Multiplication Table
question: In an m x n multiplication table (table[i][j] = i*j, 1-indexed), return the kth smallest element. Binary search on value [1, m*n]: count elements <= mid as sum of min(mid/i, n) for i in [1,m]. O(m log(mn)).

title: Find K-th Smallest Pair Distance
question: Given an integer array, define pair distance as |nums[i] - nums[j]|. Find the kth smallest distance among all C(n,2) pairs. Sort the array, binary search on distance [0, max-min], count pairs with distance <= mid using a sliding window.

title: Minimize Max Distance to Gas Station
question: Given n gas station positions on a horizontal line and integer k, add exactly k new stations to minimize the maximum distance between adjacent stations. Binary search on floating-point answer; for a candidate max distance d, check if total additional stations needed <= k.

title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
question: Given bloomDay[] where bloomDay[i] is when flower i blooms, make m bouquets each requiring k adjacent bloomed flowers. Find minimum day to make all bouquets, or return -1 if impossible. Binary search on day in [min(bloomDay), max(bloomDay)].

title: Maximum Average Subarray II
question: Given an integer array and minimum length k, find the contiguous subarray of length >= k with maximum average. Binary search on the average value; for a candidate mid, subtract mid from all elements and check if any subarray of length >= k has non-negative prefix sum.

title: Cutting Ribbons
question: Given ribbon lengths and integer k, cut ribbons so you get at least k pieces all of equal positive integer length. Maximize that length. Binary search on length [1, max(ribbons)]; for each candidate length, check if total pieces >= k by summing floor(ribbon/length).

title: Minimize Maximum of Array
question: Given an integer array, you can apply the following operation any number of times: choose index i > 0, increment nums[i-1] by 1, decrement nums[i] by 1. Minimize the maximum value of the array. Binary search on answer: check if target max is achievable by verifying prefix averages never exceed target.

title: Maximum Running Time of N Computers
question: Given n computers and batteries with given capacities, find the maximum minutes you can run all n computers simultaneously. You can swap batteries during runtime. Binary search on time t: check if total battery capacity minus extras (capped at t) >= n * t.

title: Two Sum
question: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. You may assume exactly one solution exists and you may not use the same element twice. Use a hash map for O(n) time.

title: First Non-Repeating Character
question: Given a string s, return the index of the first non-repeating character. If none exists, return -1. Use a frequency hash map: first pass counts occurrences, second pass returns the first index whose count is 1.
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters

title: Contains Duplicate
question: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and false if every element is distinct. Insert elements into a hash set and check for collisions in O(n) time.

title: Valid Anagram
question: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s and false otherwise. An anagram uses every original letter exactly once. Compare character-frequency maps built from both strings.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters

title: Intersection of Two Arrays
question: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, return an array of their intersection. Each element in the result must be unique. Use a hash set built from nums1, then collect elements of nums2 that exist in that set.

title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
question: Given an integer array of length n where all integers are in [1, n] and each integer appears once or twice, return all integers that appear twice. Aim for O(n) time with a hash set, or O(1) extra space by negating visited indices.

title: Happy Number
question: A happy number repeatedly replaces itself with the sum of squares of its digits. Return true if it eventually reaches 1, false if it loops forever. Use a hash set to detect the cycle.

title: Ransom Note
question: Given strings ransomNote and magazine, return true if ransomNote can be constructed using letters from magazine (each letter used at most once). Build a frequency map of magazine characters and check against ransomNote.
constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters

title: Word Pattern
question: Given a pattern and a space-separated string s, return true if s follows the same pattern (a bijection between each pattern character and each word in s). Use two hash maps—char→word and word→char—to enforce bidirectional uniqueness.
constraints: pattern and words in s consist of lowercase English letters

title: Isomorphic Strings
question: Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic: characters in s can be replaced to get t, preserving order, with a one-to-one mapping. Use two hash maps (s→t and t→s) to verify the bijection.
constraints: s and t consist of valid ASCII characters

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
question: Given an unsorted integer array, find the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence in O(n). Insert all numbers into a hash set; for each number whose predecessor is absent (sequence start), expand the streak and track the maximum.

title: Group Anagrams
question: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together and return them in any order. Key each group by the sorted form of the word (or a 26-element frequency tuple) in a hash map.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
question: Given an integer array nums and integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals k. Use a running prefix sum and a hash map counting each prefix sum's occurrences; for each index i, add prefixCount[runningSum - k] to the answer.

title: 4Sum II
question: Given four integer arrays A, B, C, D each of length n, count tuples (i,j,k,l) such that A[i]+B[j]+C[k]+D[l] == 0. Store all pairwise sums A[i]+B[j] in a hash map with counts, then count completions -(C[k]+D[l]) in O(n^2).

title: Top K Frequent Elements
question: Given an integer array and integer k, return the k most frequent elements in any order. Build a frequency hash map, then use bucket sort (index = frequency) or a min-heap of size k to extract the answer in O(n log k).
constraints: Answer is guaranteed to be unique

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
question: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Use a sliding window with a hash map storing the last-seen index of each character; jump the left pointer to last_seen[c]+1 on collision for O(n) time.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols, and spaces

title: Minimum Window Substring
question: Given strings s and t, return the minimum window substring of s containing all characters of t (with duplicates). Use a sliding window plus two frequency hash maps and a 'have vs need' counter to validate the window in amortised O(|s|+|t|).
constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters

title: Brick Wall
question: Given a brick wall as a list of rows (each row is a list of brick widths), draw a vertical line crossing the fewest bricks. Count interior edge positions (cumulative widths excluding the last brick) per row using a hash map; pick the most common edge. Answer = rows - max_edge_count.
constraints: sum(wall[i]) is equal for every row

title: Contiguous Array
question: Given a binary array, find the maximum length of a contiguous subarray with equal numbers of 0s and 1s. Replace 0 with -1, then track running prefix sums in a hash map of first-seen indices; whenever the same prefix sum repeats, the subarray between those indices is balanced.

title: Continuous Subarray Sum (Divisible by K)
question: Given an integer array and integer k, return true if there exists a subarray of length >= 2 whose sum is a multiple of k. Track prefix sum modulo k in a hash map of first-seen indices; two equal mod values whose indices differ by >= 2 imply a valid subarray.

title: Palindrome Pairs
question: Given a list of unique words, find all pairs (i, j) where i ≠ j such that words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome. Store all words in a hash map; for each word split into prefix/suffix, check if the reversed counterpart exists while the remaining half is itself a palindrome.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters

title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
question: Given a string s and an array words (all same length w), return all starting indices of substrings in s that are a concatenation of every word in words exactly once. For each offset in [0, w), slide a window of size words.length * w, using a frequency hash map to validate in O(|s| * w).
constraints: s and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters

title: Number of Atoms
question: Given a chemical formula string, return the count of each atom sorted by element name. Use a stack of hash maps: push a new map on '(', pop and multiply counts on ')' using any following number, merging into the map below.
constraints: formula consists of English letters, digits, '(', ')'
formula is always a valid chemical formula

title: Max Points on a Line
question: Given an array of points on a 2D plane, find the maximum number of points that lie on the same straight line. For each anchor point compute slopes to every other point as reduced fractions (using gcd of dy and dx) stored in a hash map. O(n^2).

title: Longest Duplicate Substring
question: Given a string s, find the longest substring that appears at least twice. Binary-search on the candidate length and use Rabin-Karp rolling hash to check whether any substring of that length is duplicated in O(n log n) expected time.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

title: Alien Dictionary
question: Given a list of words sorted in an alien language's lexicographic order, derive the character ordering. Compare adjacent words to extract directed edges between characters, build the graph with a hash map, then perform topological sort (BFS/Kahn). Return '' on a cycle or invalid input.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters

title: Count Subarrays with Score Less Than K
question: The score of a subarray is defined as its length multiplied by its sum. Given a positive integer array and long integer k, return the number of non-empty subarrays with score strictly less than k. Use prefix sums and binary search on the prefix sum array for each right endpoint in O(n log n).

title: Find Duplicate File in System
question: Given a list of directory info strings each formatted as 'root/d1 f1.txt(content1) f2.txt(content2)', group files with identical content. Parse each string, extract (path, content) pairs, and insert into a hash map keyed by content. Return groups with size >= 2.
constraints: paths[i] contains valid directory and file info

title: Make Sum Divisible by P
question: Given a positive integer array and integer p, remove the smallest subarray (possibly empty) so the remaining sum is divisible by p. Use prefix sum modulo p stored in a hash map of most-recent index; find a subarray whose sum ≡ totalSum % p (mod p). Return -1 if impossible.

title: Sum of Subarray Ranges
question: Given an integer array, return the sum over all subarrays of (max of subarray − min of subarray). The naive O(n^2) approach works within constraints; the optimal O(n) solution uses two monotonic stacks to compute the contribution of each element as a maximum minus its contribution as a minimum.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
question: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (the number of nodes along the longest root-to-leaf path). Use recursive DFS: depth = 1 + max(left, right), returning 0 for null nodes.

title: Symmetric Tree
question: Given the root of a binary tree, check whether it is a mirror of itself (symmetric around its centre). Use recursive DFS comparing left and right subtrees: left.val == right.val and left.left mirrors right.right and left.right mirrors right.left.

title: Invert Binary Tree
question: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree (mirror it) and return its root. Swap left and right children at every node using recursive DFS or iterative BFS.

title: Path Sum
question: Given the root of a binary tree and integer targetSum, return true if there exists a root-to-leaf path whose node values sum to targetSum. Subtract the current node's value as you recurse; return true when a leaf's remaining target is zero.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
question: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level-order traversal of its node values as a list of lists. Use a queue (BFS): at each step, process all nodes at the current depth before enqueuing their children.

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
question: Given the root of a binary tree, return the length of the tree's diameter (the longest path between any two nodes, measured in edges). At each node, the candidate diameter is leftHeight + rightHeight; track the global maximum during DFS.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
question: Given a BST and two nodes p and q, find their lowest common ancestor (LCA). Exploit the BST property: if both p and q are less than the current node, descend left; if both are greater, descend right; otherwise the current node is the LCA.
constraints: p != q, both p and q exist in the tree

title: Convert Sorted Array to Height-Balanced BST
question: Given a sorted integer array, construct a height-balanced BST. Recursively choose the middle element as the root, then build the left subtree from the left half and the right subtree from the right half.
constraints: nums is sorted in strictly ascending order

title: Count Complete Tree Nodes
question: Given the root of a complete binary tree, return the number of nodes. Leverage the complete-tree property: measure left-most and right-most depths; if equal the subtree is a perfect binary tree with 2^h - 1 nodes; otherwise recurse on both halves. O(log^2 n).
constraints: Tree is guaranteed to be complete

title: Merge Two Binary Trees
question: You are given two binary trees. Merge them: overlapping nodes sum their values; non-overlapping nodes remain as-is. Recurse simultaneously on both trees, creating new nodes where one tree has null.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each tree <= 2000

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
question: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid BST. Use in-order traversal and verify each value is strictly greater than the previous, or pass min/max bounds through recursive DFS.

title: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
question: Given the root of a binary tree, return the zigzag level-order traversal: alternate between left-to-right and right-to-left for successive levels. Use BFS with a flag that reverses the current level's list before appending.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
question: Given the preorder and inorder traversal arrays of a binary tree, reconstruct and return the tree. The first element of preorder is always the root; find its index in inorder to split into left and right subtrees. Use a hash map for O(1) inorder lookup.

title: Path Sum II – All Root-to-Leaf Paths
question: Given a binary tree and integer targetSum, return all root-to-leaf paths where the sum of the values equals targetSum. Use DFS with backtracking: add the current node to the path, recurse, then remove it. Copy the path to results only at a valid leaf.

title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
question: Given the root of a binary tree, flatten it to a linked list in-place in preorder. Set each node's right pointer to its preorder successor and left pointer to null. Use Morris traversal (O(1) space) or a reverse-preorder DFS approach.

title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
question: Implement an iterator over a BST's in-order traversal. Support next() (return the next smallest value) and hasNext() (return whether a next element exists). Use an explicit stack, pushing left-spine nodes lazily for O(h) average space and O(1) average time per call.
constraints: At most 10^5 calls to hasNext and next

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
question: Given the root of a BST and integer k, return the kth smallest value. Perform an in-order DFS (left → root → right) counting nodes; return the value when the counter equals k. O(H + k) time where H is the tree height.

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
question: Given the root of a binary tree, imagine standing on the right side. Return the values of the nodes you can see top-to-bottom (the last node of each level). Use BFS and pick the last element of each level, or DFS visiting right before left.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
question: Given a general binary tree (not a BST) and two nodes p and q, find their lowest common ancestor. Use post-order DFS: if the current node equals p or q, return it; combine results from left and right subtrees—if both are non-null the current node is the LCA.
constraints: p and q both exist in the tree

title: Recover Binary Search Tree
question: Exactly two nodes of a BST are swapped by mistake. Recover the tree without changing its structure. In-order traverse and find the two violated nodes (first where prev > current, second is the current at the first violation or a later violation); then swap their values.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
question: Given a binary tree, find the path with the maximum sum. The path can start and end at any node. At each node during DFS, the local contribution is node.val + max(0, left_gain) + max(0, right_gain); return node.val + max(0, better_child) up the chain. Track the global maximum.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
question: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize that string back to the original tree. Use BFS (level-order) or preorder with 'null' markers; split on a delimiter and reconstruct the tree using a queue or pointer.

title: Binary Tree Cameras
question: Place cameras on some nodes of a binary tree so that every node is monitored (a camera monitors its parent, itself, and its children). Minimise the number of cameras. Use a greedy post-order DFS with three states per node: 0 = needs coverage, 1 = covered (no camera), 2 = has camera.

title: Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
question: Given a binary tree, return its vertical-order traversal. Assign column/row coordinates via DFS; group nodes by column (ties broken by row then by value). Return groups sorted from leftmost to rightmost column.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
question: Given an integer array nums, for each element count how many elements to its right are smaller. Process from right to left, inserting each number into a BST augmented with subtree sizes; count nodes in the left subtree (values less than current) at each insertion.

title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
question: Given a binary tree, return the maximum width of any level. Width is the number of nodes between (and including) the leftmost and rightmost non-null nodes. Assign positional indices to nodes (root=1, left child=2i, right child=2i+1); max width at each BFS level is last_index - first_index + 1.

title: Distribute Coins in Binary Tree
question: Each node in a binary tree contains a number of coins; total coins equals the number of nodes. Return the minimum number of moves to give exactly one coin to each node. Each move transfers one coin along an edge. The number of moves equals the sum of absolute excess at each subtree root (|coins_in_subtree - nodes_in_subtree|).
constraints: sum of all Node.val equals number of nodes

title: Sum of Distances in Tree
question: Given an unweighted tree with n nodes, return an array where answer[i] is the sum of distances from node i to every other node. Perform two DFS passes: first compute subtree sizes and distances from root 0; then re-root using the identity answer[child] = answer[parent] - count[child] + (n - count[child]).

title: Find the Centre of a Star Graph
question: There is an undirected star graph with n nodes (1-indexed) and n-1 edges, where one centre node is connected to every other node. Given the edge list, return the centre node. The centre appears in every edge, so it must appear in both the first and second edge.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
question: Given n nodes (0 to n-1) and a list of undirected edges, return the number of connected components. Use DFS or BFS from each unvisited node, incrementing the component counter each time a new traversal starts.

title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
question: Given an undirected graph with n nodes and an edge list, determine if there is a valid path from source to destination. Use BFS or DFS from the source; return true if the destination is reached.

title: Flood Fill
question: Given an image represented as a 2D integer grid and a starting pixel (sr, sc), perform a flood fill: recolor the starting pixel and all 4-directionally connected pixels of the same original color to the new color. Use DFS or BFS.

title: Island Perimeter
question: Given a grid where 1 = land and 0 = water, return the perimeter of the island (guaranteed to be exactly one island with no lakes). For each land cell, start with 4 sides and subtract 1 for each adjacent land neighbour.

title: Number of Islands
question: Given a 2D binary grid of '1's (land) and '0's (water), count the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent land cells (4-directionally). Use DFS or BFS marking visited cells.

title: Maximum Depth of Island
question: Given a 2D binary grid of 0s and 1s, return the area of the largest island (the maximum number of 1s in a 4-directionally connected component). Use DFS/BFS, marking visited cells as 0, and track each component's size.

title: Clone Graph
question: Given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the graph. Use BFS or DFS with a hash map that maps each original node to its clone; build neighbour lists as you traverse.
constraints: Node.val is unique for each node
There are no repeated edges or self-loops

title: All Paths from Source to Target
question: Given a directed acyclic graph (DAG) with n nodes, find all paths from node 0 to node n-1 and return them in any order. Use DFS with backtracking: add the current node, recurse into all neighbours, and if node n-1 is reached save a copy of the path.

title: Time Needed to Inform All Employees
question: A company has n employees (0-indexed). Given headID (head manager), a manager array, and informTime array, find the total time to inform all employees of news. Build a tree from manager[] and DFS from the head; each path cost is the sum of informTime along the path. Return the maximum.

title: Number of Provinces
question: Given an n×n adjacency matrix isConnected, return the number of provinces (groups of directly or indirectly connected cities). Use DFS or Union-Find: traverse each unvisited city, marking all reachable cities as the same province.

title: Course Schedule (Cycle Detection)
question: Given numCourses and prerequisites (each [a,b] means b must be taken before a), determine if you can finish all courses. Detect whether the directed graph has a cycle using DFS with three states (unvisited / visiting / done) or BFS Kahn's topological sort.

title: Course Schedule II (Topological Sort)
question: Given numCourses and prerequisites, return one valid order to finish all courses, or [] if impossible. Perform topological sort via BFS (Kahn's algorithm): collect in-degree-0 nodes, process them in order, and verify all courses were processed.

title: Rotting Oranges
question: In a grid, 0 = empty, 1 = fresh orange, 2 = rotten orange. Each minute, every fresh orange 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten one becomes rotten. Return the minimum minutes to rot all fresh oranges, or -1 if impossible. Use multi-source BFS from all initially rotten cells.

title: 01 Matrix (BFS Distance to Nearest 0)
question: Given a binary matrix, return a matrix of the same size where each cell contains the distance to the nearest 0. Use multi-source BFS: initialise the queue with all 0-cells at distance 0, then expand layer by layer to update distances for 1-cells.

title: Graph Valid Tree
question: Given n nodes labelled 0 to n-1 and an undirected edge list, determine if the edges form a valid tree. A tree has exactly n-1 edges and is fully connected with no cycles. Use Union-Find (reject a union of already-connected nodes) or DFS.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
question: Given an m×n height matrix, water can flow to 4-adjacent cells of equal or lower height. Find all cells from which water can flow to both the Pacific ocean (top/left border) and Atlantic ocean (bottom/right border). Multi-source BFS/DFS backwards from each ocean border.

title: Surrounded Regions
question: Given an m×n grid of 'X' and 'O', capture surrounded regions: flip all 'O's that are not on or connected to the border to 'X'. Multi-source DFS/BFS from border 'O' cells, marking them safe; then flip all remaining unmarked 'O's.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
question: Given n cities, a list of flights [from, to, price], a source src, destination dst, and integer k, find the cheapest price to fly from src to dst with at most k stops. Use Bellman-Ford for k+1 relaxation rounds, or modified Dijkstra/BFS tracking both cost and stops.

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
question: Given an undirected graph as an adjacency list, determine if it is bipartite (can be 2-coloured such that no two adjacent nodes share a colour). BFS/DFS: assign alternating colours; if two adjacent nodes share a colour, return false.

title: Word Ladder
question: Given beginWord, endWord, and a wordList, return the minimum number of transformations from beginWord to endWord where each step changes exactly one letter and the result must be in wordList. Use BFS; represent each word as a graph node and connect words differing by one letter.
constraints: All words consist of lowercase English letters
All words in wordList are unique

title: Critical Connections in a Network
question: Given n servers and a list of connections, return all critical connections (bridges) whose removal disconnects the network. Use Tarjan's bridge-finding algorithm with DFS: track discovery time and lowest reachable time; an edge (u,v) is a bridge if low[v] > disc[u].

title: Reconstruct Itinerary
question: Given a list of airline tickets [from, to], reconstruct the itinerary starting from 'JFK' that uses all tickets exactly once in lexicographical order. Use Hierholzer's algorithm for Eulerian path: DFS greedily choosing the lexicographically smallest next destination; append to result in post-order.
constraints: All strings consist of uppercase English letters
At least one valid itinerary is guaranteed

title: Minimum Cost to Connect All Points
question: Given an array of points on a 2D plane, find the minimum cost to connect all points where the cost of connecting two points is their Manhattan distance. This is a Minimum Spanning Tree problem—solve with Prim's (O(n^2)) or Kruskal's + Union-Find.
constraints: No two points are the same

title: Swim in Rising Water
question: On an n×n grid, grid[i][j] is the elevation at that cell. You can swim to adjacent cells; you can only enter a cell when the water level >= its elevation. Find the minimum time T when a path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) exists where all cells on the path have elevation <= T. Use Dijkstra's or binary search + BFS/DFS.

title: Alien Dictionary (Graph Topological Sort)
question: Given a list of words sorted in an alien language's order, determine the order of characters. Extract ordering constraints from adjacent word comparisons to build a directed graph, then perform Kahn's BFS topological sort. Return '' if a cycle exists or if a longer word appears before its prefix.
constraints: All characters are lowercase English letters

title: Network Delay Time (Dijkstra's Algorithm)
question: Given n nodes (1-indexed), directed edges [u,v,w], and a source node k, return the time for all nodes to receive the signal, or -1 if some node is unreachable. Run Dijkstra's algorithm from k; the answer is the maximum shortest-path distance, or -1 if any node remains at infinity.

title: Redundant Connection II
question: In a directed graph of n nodes with n edges, one extra edge creates a cycle or gives a node two parents, corrupting the tree. Find and return the redundant edge. Handle three cases: (1) a node with two parents and a cycle, (2) a node with two parents and no cycle, (3) only a cycle with no double-parent node.

title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
question: Given an undirected graph with n nodes, find the shortest path length that visits every node at least once (you may revisit nodes and edges). Use BFS over states (currentNode, visitedMask) where visitedMask is a bitmask of visited nodes; initialise queue with all single-node states.

title: House Robber III
question: A thief robs houses arranged in a binary tree. Adjacent nodes are directly linked; he cannot rob directly-linked houses. Return the maximum amount he can rob. For each node compute (rob_this, skip_this): rob_this = node.val + skip_left + skip_right; skip_this = max(rob_l, skip_l) + max(rob_r, skip_r).

title: Find Duplicate Subtrees
question: Given the root of a binary tree, find all duplicate subtrees. Two subtrees are duplicates if they have the same structure and node values. Serialize each subtree (post-order string) into a hash map; add the root to results the first time a serialization appears twice.

title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
question: Given a directed acyclic graph with n nodes (0-indexed) and edges, find the smallest set of vertices from which all nodes in the graph are reachable. A node can be a starting point if and only if its in-degree is 0 (no edges point into it).
